thread:
tom: Heads-up: we still see ambiguous handoffs between runtime and control-plane for dedicated customers. Observed symptom: two runners briefly accept traffic during node failover. Need a lightweight handback protocol.

nina: Agreed. My draft idea: a two-step "intent -> ack" flow instead of a long-lived lease. Sequence: runtime asks for IntentToServe, CP responds with IntentToken + grace_window. Runtime serves, then CP may request Handback; runtime replies HandbackAck within grace_window and drains or accepts redirect.

carl: Flow sketch:
```
POST /intents { tenant, runtime } -> { intent_id, grace_sec }
POST /handbacks { intent_id } -> { status: queued | acked }
GET /intents/{id} -> { holder, expires_at, state }
```
Make grace_sec small (10-60s) and require runtime to expose a drain endpoint.

maria: This differs from leases because intent is reversible quickly and CP can return 409 if another runtime already has intent. If CP cannot reach both, it returns 202 + "continue-serving" to avoid double-stop.

nina: Important: include a "quiesce" flag on handback to indicate whether in-flight requests must finish or be redirected immediately. Example: { handback_ack: true, quiesce: true, drain_deadline: 12 }

carl: For dedicated we probably want CP to prefer issuing intent to the runtime with highest residency score, but allow the runtime to renew intent if it has recent activity. Renewal windows should be jittered to avoid stampede.

maria: Ops concerns: need audit events for intent_granted, intent_revoked, handback_requested, handback_acked, handback_timeout. Also surface a metric: double-serve-seconds for billing reconciliation.

nina: Security: use short-lived signed intent tokens. Validation is local; token contains tenant, runtime, issued_at, expires_at, signature. Private mode: customer CP signs their own intents with their key. Hosted/dedicated: our CP signs.

carl: Edge case: split-brain when both sides think they have intent due to clock skew. Mitigation: require monotonic sequence number in token and CP to prefer higher sequence. Also prefer wall-clock expiry with small drift tolerance.

maria: Ops playbook idea: if double-serve detected, auto-trigger handback with quiesce=true to minimize user impact, then run postmortem on the metric.

ops-bot: incident-check: no active incidents matching "double-serve". Canary job queued: infra/intent-proto -> staging started 1765020100

tom: Action items:
- nina: write RFC for Intent/Handback proto + token format + sample SDK behavior.
- carl: simulate failure modes and measure double-serve-seconds; propose safe defaults for grace_sec.
- maria: define audit events and billing reconciliation hooks.
We should sync next Tue. :calendar:
